item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q017_prp8_evolutionary_mosaic","answer":"SCOPe decomposes Prp8 in 3jb9 into an evolutionary mosaic of five structural domains: a Prp8-specific N-terminal/linker scaffold, a reverse-transcriptase-like domain (with the associated thumb/X region), a type-II-restriction-endonuclease-like domain, an RNase-H-like domain, and a C-terminal Jab1/MPN domain. The RT-like domain has superfamily-level homology to reverse transcriptases, especially group-II-intron maturases; together with the neighboring endonuclease-like architecture, it supports descent from an ancestral group-II-intron-encoded protein. The Jab1/MPN domain is homologous to the established MPN/JAMM superfamily, whereas the endonuclease-like and RNase-H-like domains show established fold-level relationships to their named nuclease folds. Those structural matches do not justify transferring nuclease or deubiquitinase activity: Prp8 representatives lack or alter important catalytic features and mainly serve spliceosomal structural/regulatory roles. The Prp8 N-terminal/linker scaffold is the newly observed fold in this decomposition—meaning that SCOPe lacked a previously characterized structural representative, not that the domain necessarily has no remote evolutionary relatives. Thus 3jb9 supports a group-II-intron-derived core augmented by additional, sometimes catalytically repurposed domains and a Prp8-specific structural innovation; templates should be selected domain by domain rather than treating full-length Prp8 as homologous to any one of the comparison proteins.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
